title: We’re a tiny team from Berlin trying to rethink how games get made
author: val_yougotit
selftext:
Hey everyone! We’re a 3 people team from Berlin building [Jamboree](http://jamboree.app), and I’d genuinely love some feedback from you all here.

**The idea is pretty simple:** what if making a game could feel less like opening a dry game engine and more like just… having fun?

We’ve been building a mobile game editor where anyone can make a playable mini game end-to-end directly on their phone.

**You can:**

* create characters, objects, backgrounds + sounds
* create and edit animations
* change gameplay, movement, controls, camera, speed, etc.
* tap pretty much anything in your game and edit it visually
* use reference images / drawings as input
* publish it instantly for other people to play

There’s also a feed of games made by the community, so creation and playing live in the same place.

**It’s 100% free. No ads, no subscription, no IAP.**

We’ve put a ridiculous amount of work into the editor over the last few months and would really love to hear what actual AI game devs think of it.

**Especially curious:**  
What feels surprisingly good?  
What feels limiting?  
What would stop you from actually making something with it?

Try it here and let me know what you think: 

Happy to answer technical/product questions too. :)

comments.author: w1a1s1p
comments.body: Didn't try the game, but based on the trailer I think it can be a great educational tool, similar to the coding games for kids that are block based and not code writing based. Well done

replies.author: val_yougotit
replies.body: thanks so much! we can def see already that kids and teens love to create with it and are getting to really cool results pretty quickly :) let me know if you have more thoughts once you tried it!

comments.author: Alon_David
comments.body: I think it has potential if you lean more into child education with it. But I personally don’t see other demographics using it more than once.

replies.author: val_yougotit
replies.body: thanks for your feedback. why do you think so? have you tried the app or just seen the post?
